title: Evidence for an upper cretaceous strandline deposit in the Lance Formation, Wyoming, USA
content:
by Keith Snyder, Nelson Llempen, Caleb Darling, Alessandro Franchini, Matthew McLain, Arthur Chadwick

A series of apparently related quarries in the Maastrichtian (uppermost Cretaceous) Lance Formation of Wyoming provided the opportunity to evaluate the taphonomic mode for a suite of vertebrate fossils. Extensive work on the Hanson Ranch over the past three decades has exposed tens of thousands of fossils from dinosaur-bearing bonebeds. All of these bonebeds consist of disarticulated and disassociated remains. However, seven recently discovered quarries have yielded the remains of one or more dinosaur taxa (e.g., Triceratops, Edmontosaurus, Thescelosaurus, Anzu) in a state of association that was hitherto unknown on the ranch. These seven quarries were found along a line heading approximately 140 degrees, a heading reflected in the long axes of many of the elongate bones in the quarries. The preservation of associated remains suggests that soft-tissue connections or integumentary containment persisted during the transport and burial. We conclude that the floating, encapsulated carcasses of these animals were stranded along a southeasterly trending shoreline of the Western Interior Seaway.
author: Keith Snyder
